label: late original-phase input of x/i/l/h-type tokens, in sequences starting with k/t/j/g/a/p/e/r
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase at late positions (orig_idx >= 5; 99% of mass), so mostly in long sequences (L = 8-9). It never fires in the copy phase and barely fires on the delimiter. Firing rate climbs with position, from 2.5% at orig_idx 5 to 16% at orig_idx 8. The current input token matters: x is strongest (6x lift, and the top examples are mostly x), then i, l, h, then 1, c, v, d. The firing also depends on which tokens came earlier, especially the first token (k, t, j, g, a, p, e, r raise the rate). These factors seem to add up gradually rather than act as a sharp conjunction, so no clean predicate gets past dev F1 of about 0.5. Late original position alone has recall 0.98 but precision 0.07.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=6: x, i, l, h; t=7: x, i, l, h; t=8: x, l, i, h) and the first original token (most: k, t, j, g, p, a; least: 1, h, l, x); timing cues that raise it most: t=6, L=9 & t=8, t=7.
